newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Hang Seng ends above 13,000 for first time. [CORRECTED 13:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng ends above 13,000 for first time. [CORRECTED 13:10 GMT]

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index closed above 13,000 points for the first time ever on Thursday, driven by optimism about interest rates and the property market, analysts said.
The index closed 61.11 points higher at 13,004.80 after hitting a record intraday high at 13,009.74. Turnover was HK$8.22 billion compared with HK$7.83 billion on Wednesday.
"It was led by several large property counters," said Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International. "People revalued and probably rerated them again and you see aggressive buying today."

Wednesday's government land auction -- where a 4,206-square-metre plot was sold for HK$370 million, well above expectations of HK$260 million to HK$320 million -- revived optimism about the outlook for the property market.
"Many analysts predict that in 1997, residential prices may continue to go higher," said Tang.
The U.S. Federal Reserve's decision on Wednesday to leave interest rates unchanged added to the positive sentiment.
"In the medium-to-long term, the market is still not expensive," said Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities.
"It may be technically overbought but, based on 1997 earnings, it is at 13.5 times so it is not expensive in comparison with other Asian markets," he added.
So said the market was likely to benefit from earnings upgrades due to strength in the property market and stronger retail sales. "That suggests further upside," he said.
But analysts said investors may be tempted to take profits at current levels, particularly if Wall Street stocks consolidate or the U.S. long bond yield inches up.
"But if the long bond yield continues to decline, there will be still momentum in the market," said So.
He saw the Hang Seng meeting resistance at around 12,200 points (Corrects from 13,200 points).
Shares in Sun Hung Kai Properties led gains in the property sector, rising HK$2.25 to HK$92.00. Cheung Kong rose HK$0.75 to HK$67.00 and Henderson Land advanced HK$0.25 to HK$71.50.
Conglomerates also made gains, with Swire Pacific rising HK$1.00 to HK$69.25 and Wharf Holdings up HK$0.40 at HK$35.00. Shares in Wheelock rose HK$0.45 to HK$19.65.
Banks failed to participate in Thursday's advance. HSBC Holdings finished unchanged at HK$162.00 and Hang Seng Bank also closed flat at HK$96.25. -- Jennifer Genevieve (852) 2843 6345
